Do people actually pay attention to video game awards? Just play what's good, all the awards are bought anyway.

I think it was Yahtzee who's been calling Openworld the new default genre. And before that it was knee high wall cover shooter, and before that it was quake style shooter. For a year or two it was RTS. In the early, early days I hear it was PC adaptations of tabletop wargames.

There are definitely booms and busts for the different genres. It's been a long, long time since I saw an RPG in the tradition of Gold Box or Infinity Engine in the running. Although thank god we are getting more of them at least. I've also not seen a good simulation game in the tradition of Mechwarrior, Interstate 76 or the dozens of Flight Sims that used to be a staple of PC Gaming. And let's not forget RTS, which had an enormous boom and bust leading up to the release of StarCraft. That game was in development so long, people were desperate for anything that looked like StarCraft, but was out NOW. I remember an issue of Computer Gaming World where they covered 100 different RTSes in development!

I'll always have a soft spot for Dark Reign, that game was so easily moddable.

I'm looking forward to the Open World Boom to turn into a bust. I doubt we'll get our old genres back the way we deserve them. But maybe in 5 years time, you'll see Open World Game: The Open World Game hat in hand on Kickstarter asking for a few nostalgia bucks, because nobody makes them like they used to anymore.
